postconditions.expression: all(len(s) == n for n, s in zip(n_values, s_values))
postconditions.description: Each string s has length n as specified.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= k <= n <= 10^6 for n, k in zip(n_values, k_values))
postconditions.description: The length of the string s and the length k are within the specified bounds.

postconditions.expression: all(all(c in '01' for c in s) for s in s_values)
postconditions.description: Each character in the string s is either 0 or 1.

postconditions.expression: all(any(s[i] == s[i+j] for i in range(n-k+1)) for j in range(1, k))
postconditions.description: For each substring of length k, there exists at least one position where the characters match.

postconditions.expression: all(any(t[i] == s[i+j] for i in range(k)) for j in range(n-k+1))
postconditions.description: For each position in the beautiful string t, there exists a corresponding position in the string s where the characters match.

postconditions.expression: all(t == min(t for t in possible_beauties) for possible_beauties in all_possible_beauties)
postconditions.description: The lexicographically smallest beautiful string is found.

invariants.expression: all(len(t) == k for t in possible_beauties)
invariants.description: All possible beautiful strings have length k.

invariants.expression: all(all(c in '01' for c in t) for t in possible_beauties)
invariants.description: All characters in all possible beautiful strings are either 0 or 1.
